name: Classroom Words
purpose: Phonics games and controlled decodable text matched to the sounds already taught by the classroom teacher.
guardrail: Only use s a t p i n as the taught graphemes in this example; child reading text must be decodable with those letters. Navigation labels may use normal adult English. Avoid generic spelling practice.

directions.title: Sound tiles
directions.tagline: Small sounds. Words to grow on.
directions.style: Warm ivory #F8F1DF, petrol #164C51, marigold #EDBD4F. Tactile letter tiles, round humanist typography, a spacious tabletop.
directions.screen: Title Make a word. Three large tiles s a t, sound dots and blending arc. Your sounds panel s a t p i n, Set by your teacher. Hear the sounds and Blend the word buttons.
directions.logo: Two slightly overlapping lowercase c and w letter tiles, petrol c tile and marigold w tile, small joining arc.

directions.title: Reading garden
directions.tagline: Practise the sounds you know.
directions.style: Sage #E3EBCF, forest #244D38, poppy #C4593C. Cut-paper garden, friendly open rounded type, low horizontal navigation.
directions.screen: A garden path of three word stepping stones: sat, pin, tap. Main task Tap the word you hear. Speaker button Hear it again. Side strip Your sounds: s a t p i n. No pictures revealing the answer. One quiet little plant marks progress.
directions.logo: An open book whose two pages become paired sprouting leaves, with three small sound dots underneath.

directions.title: Sound station
directions.tagline: Your classroom sounds, ready to play.
directions.style: Chalk white #F5F3EC, brick #A84432, muted cobalt #345B89. Printed railway tickets and a bold geometric type family.
directions.screen: Word-building station with three coupled carriages showing p i n. Heading Join the sounds. Bottom platform holds letter tickets s a t p i n. Large Hear each sound and Read the word controls. Teacher set visible as a small top badge.
directions.logo: Three train-ticket shapes join to form a compact W, with a small sound-wave cutout in the first ticket.

directions.title: Little reading room
directions.tagline: A little practice. A new word.
directions.style: Butter #F4DE9F, ink #293C52, soft blue #BCD4DD. Calm storybook spread, generous rounded lettering and linen borders.
directions.screen: Large two-page reading spread with strictly decodable text Pat sat. and a gentle illustration of a seated child on the other page. Heading Read with your sounds. Large Listen, Try reading and Next page buttons. Small teacher-set sounds s a t p i n.
directions.logo: Two facing book pages form a cosy doorway, a small sun dot above the centre fold.

directions.title: Sound circles
directions.tagline: Hear it. Build it. Read it.
directions.style: Mint #D9EEE5, dark teal #164F4C, peach #F4B090. Extremely clean touch-first concentric sound circles and broad rounded typography.
directions.screen: Centred three large sound circles t a p connected by a line. Heading Blend these sounds. One huge central Listen button, a lower three-choice word row tap, pin, sat. Footer My sounds: s a t p i n. Very little decorative content.
directions.logo: Three connected circles form a speech bubble with a short tail; alternating solid and open circles suggest blending.

name: Think in Parts
purpose: A multimodal explanation studio where students draw, animate, record voice and build interactive diagrams; teachers set structured challenges and assess reasoning.
guardrail: Show a student-authored explanation, not automatic AI answers. Include a clear assignment or explanation goal.

directions.title: Paper mechanism
directions.tagline: Make your thinking visible.
directions.style: Warm paper #F3EBDD, charcoal #263C3B, burnt orange #BB6239. Folded-paper diagrams, editorial serif headings with clean humanist controls.
directions.screen: Canvas title How does a lever work? A labelled lever with fulcrum, effort and load. Left tools Draw, Label, Record. Bottom four-frame animation timeline. Right challenge Explain what changes when the fulcrum moves. Buttons Preview and Hand in.
directions.logo: Three folded geometric pieces assemble into a speech bubble, with one orange piece slightly separated.

directions.title: Motion bench
directions.tagline: Build an explanation that moves.
directions.style: Storm blue #D5E1E7, ink #203D53, rust #B85739. Animation workbench with tactile frame strips and technical but friendly type.
directions.screen: Centre a student-drawn water cycle with arrows. Heading Why does rain fall? Bottom storyboard Evaporation, Condensation, Rain. A voice waveform under each frame; right inspector Arrow motion and Duration. Assignment panel Explain each change. Preview explanation button.
directions.logo: Three offset film frames form a forward arrow, one containing a simple speech bubble.

directions.title: Idea atlas
directions.tagline: Connect the parts. Explain the whole.
directions.style: Bone #F1EFD9, olive #4B603C, plum ink #583F58. Spacious node canvas with organic connectors and atlas-like typography.
directions.screen: Concept map titled What keeps an ecosystem balanced? Linked nodes Plants, Insects, Birds, Water. Selected connection opens My explanation with a recorded audio strip. Left challenge drawer Use two cause-and-effect links. Bottom tools Sketch, Voice, Connect.
directions.logo: Four irregular map-like pieces fit into a circular whole, a small visible gap marks the connection point.

directions.title: Voice and ink
directions.tagline: Draw it out. Talk it through.
directions.style: Soft white #F6F3EB, bottle green #25574C, salmon #D88D73. Minimal sketchbook studio, inky drawn annotations, asymmetric margin notes.
directions.screen: Large hand-drawn circuit with battery, switch and bulb. Title Why does the bulb light? Visible voice recording waveform and 00:24 timer beneath canvas. Left small drawing tool rail; right prompt Explain the complete path. Buttons Listen back and Add a label.
directions.logo: A single confident line becomes both a pencil stroke and an audio waveform within an open speech mark.

directions.title: Exhibit studio
directions.tagline: Show how your idea works.
directions.style: Cream #F5E8CF, deep blue #2C4369, ochre #C39A38. Museum exhibit panels, elegant display serif, restrained interactive diagram controls.
directions.screen: Student exhibit titled How a bridge shares a load. Main interactive bridge diagram with a Load slider and highlighted supports. Three tabs Model, Explain, Reflect. Teacher brief Use your model to explain a force. Small narration panel and Test my explanation button.
directions.logo: A compact open display plinth holds three distinct shapes, with a small speech arc above them.

name: Town Together
purpose: A simulated council or parliament where students investigate an issue, compare competing proposals, manage a budget and justify a decision.
guardrail: Use a fictional town and clearly labelled simulated budget in Australian dollars. Trade-offs and justification matter; do not reduce democracy to popularity points.

directions.title: Council table
directions.tagline: Big decisions. Different voices.
directions.style: Paper #F4EBD9, forest #244D3D, ochre #CCA148. Tactile tabletop town model and council-paper side panels, mature rounded sans.
directions.screen: A small illustrated town square in centre. Heading A new life for the old oval. Proposal panels Community garden A$20,000 and Sports upgrade A$30,000. Simulated budget A$30,000. Tabs Hear residents, Compare, Decide. Primary Build our recommendation.
directions.logo: Three different roof shapes surround an open central circle, suggesting a shared meeting table.

directions.title: Neighbourhood newsroom
directions.tagline: Every proposal has a story.
directions.style: Newsprint #F0E6D0, brick #AC4434, ink #292F35. Editorial newspaper grid, large serif headlines, illustrated local reportage.
directions.screen: Headline What should happen to the creek? A prominent illustrated creek map, resident quotation cards and two competing proposal columns. Evidence notebook in right margin. Simulated budget A$40,000. Buttons Compare proposals and Write our reasons.
directions.logo: A folded newspaper corner becomes a pair of neighbouring rooftops; one open speech notch.

directions.title: Town blueprint
directions.tagline: Plan a place. Weigh the choices.
directions.style: Pale blue #DBE6E8, dark blue #264A60, warm orange #CB783E. Clean planning-map aesthetic, thin map lines, bold utilitarian headings.
directions.screen: Top-down town plan with highlighted crossing, library and park. Heading Safer journeys to school. Toggle proposals Raised crossing A$18,000, New footpath A$24,000. Budget A$30,000. Side panel Who benefits? Who misses out? Button Explain our choice.
directions.logo: Two interlocking street-grid T shapes form a shared square with one warm orange meeting point.

directions.title: People’s assembly
directions.tagline: Listen widely. Decide together.
directions.style: Pale peach #F1DCCA, aubergine ink #4A3544, sage #91AB8E. Semicircular chamber, printed portrait tokens, humanist display lettering.
directions.screen: Fictional assembly room arranged in a semicircle. Heading A library open after school? Three resident perspectives visible: Student, Librarian, Local trader. Right panel Proposal, Cost, Trade-offs. Simulated budget A$25,000. Buttons Ask a question and Draft our decision.
directions.logo: Five distinct rounded marks make an open semicircle around a central speech bubble.

directions.title: Common ground
directions.tagline: Find the reasons behind a decision.
directions.style: Linen #EFEDE3, teal #205B59, ochre #D8AD53. Community noticeboard with pinned evidence and hand-marked links, restrained block type.
directions.screen: Decision board title Shade for the town centre. Left Evidence: Summer temperatures and Resident survey. Centre two illustrated options Trees and Shade sails. Right budget comparison A$15,000 versus A$22,000 with available A$25,000. Bottom Our reasons writing field.
directions.logo: Two overlapping irregular land shapes create a shared speech-shaped space at their intersection.

name: Wild Notebook
purpose: School-ground biodiversity, weather, water and habitat missions combining outdoor observation, data comparison and classroom discussion.
guardrail: Observations are student records, not guaranteed species identification. Show uncertain observations honestly. Keep field tasks feasible in school grounds.

directions.title: Field journal
directions.tagline: Look closer. Find more.
directions.style: Oat #F4EBD5, fern #34513A, rust #B75D39. Botanical field journal, fine specimen drawings and elegant serif headings.
directions.screen: Open field journal titled Who lives under the leaves? Left illustrated leaf-litter observation with caption Unidentified beetle. Right structured entries Location: school garden, Count: 3, Notes. Bottom Add photo, Sketch, Record voice. Small button labelled Compare with our class.
directions.logo: An open notebook with a single leaf-shaped page and a small observation dot.

directions.title: Expedition map
directions.tagline: Science starts outside.
directions.style: Pale sage #DDE8D9, ink #284B47, mustard #C2A043. Tactile school-ground map, stamped mission numbers and clean round sans.
directions.screen: School-ground map with three observation points Garden, Oval, Drain. Selected mission Where does rainwater go? Right panel Prediction and Record an observation. Bottom session strip Observe, Compare, Discuss. Large Start field notes button.
directions.logo: A winding observation route forms a W inside a folded field-map outline.

directions.title: Pocket observatory
directions.tagline: Notice a change. Ask a question.
directions.style: Cloud #E6EBE8, storm #304D63, copper #BB764A. Calm weather instrument aesthetic with precise numerals and soft circular gauges.
directions.screen: Title Is the shady spot cooler? Two sample locations Sun and Shade, student sample readings 24 °C and 20 °C, clearly labelled Example observations. A time-series comparison chart with labelled axes. Bottom Add reading and Discuss the pattern. Pencil note Same time, same thermometer.
directions.logo: A leaf and a small sun orbit a notebook-shaped centre, in one simple balanced instrument mark.

directions.title: Habitat layers
directions.tagline: Small places. Living questions.
directions.style: Sand #EEDFC5, moss #45613C, terracotta #BA6548. Layered paper-cut soil cross-section, organic panels and warm compact sans.
directions.screen: School garden cross-section with leaf litter, soil and roots. Heading Compare two habitats. Side-by-side observation trays Garden bed and Paved edge with student counts. Prompt What might explain the difference? Buttons Add evidence and Class discussion.
directions.logo: Three stacked organic strata form an open book, with a small sprout emerging from the top layer.

directions.title: Evidence collection
directions.tagline: Bring the outdoors into the discussion.
directions.style: Ivory #F1F1E5, dark petrol #22515A, muted coral #CE795E. Specimen collection trays, fine ruled labels and photographic-style botanical illustration.
directions.screen: An observation collection with four labelled field records, leaf, insect, cloud and puddle. Heading What did our class notice? A selected leaf record shows Sketch, Location, Questions. Bottom comparison tray Morning and Afternoon. Button Compare observations.
directions.logo: Four field-note corners make a viewfinder, enclosing a single asymmetrical leaf.

name: TinkerTest
purpose: A virtual investigation lab for choosing variables, predicting, running experiments and interpreting results when physical experiments are impractical.
guardrail: Clearly identify simulation and illustrative data. Isolate one independent variable and preserve controls. Do not present simulated outcomes as real measurements.

directions.title: Workshop lab
directions.tagline: Change one thing. Discover what happens.
directions.style: Warm grey #ECE9DE, petrol #22505A, orange #C8753D. Matte instrument bench, substantial controls, clean scientific typography.
directions.screen: Simulation: Ramp investigation. A ball on adjustable ramp, independent variable Ramp height, controls Same ball and Same surface. Prediction field I think... Run test button. Results table with height 10, 20, 30 cm and simulated distance 28, 49, 71 cm. Clearly label Simulated results.
directions.logo: A laboratory flask contains one adjustable slider track with an orange variable dot.

directions.title: Test track
directions.tagline: Predict it. Run it. Rethink it.
directions.style: Pale mint #DDEBDD, midnight green #284E40, warm yellow #D3B34A. Top-down experiment track, wide horizontal controls and striking numeric typography.
directions.screen: Friction simulation with three parallel lanes Felt, Wood, Sandpaper. Same trolley and same ramp controls locked. Heading Which surface slows it most? Prediction selection above track; results empty ready state Run a trial to compare distance. Large Run trial and Reset buttons.
directions.logo: Three parallel track lines converge into a question-mark-shaped route, with one movable test dot.

directions.title: Variable studio
directions.tagline: A good question deserves a fair test.
directions.style: Bone #F4EFDF, burgundy #653E45, sage #95A48C. Scientific notebook mixed with modular variable blocks, scholarly serif headings.
directions.screen: Heading Does light change plant growth? Label Virtual investigation. Three model plants under labelled light conditions Low, Medium, High. Control chips Same water, Same soil, Same time. Left My prediction; right simulated growth chart. Button Compare trials.
directions.logo: Three plant-like bars of different heights emerge from a single baseline beneath a small adjustment dial.

directions.title: Glasshouse
directions.tagline: Try the experiment you imagined.
directions.style: Soft blue #DEEBED, forest #285443, clay #BD7758. Architectural glasshouse diagrams, airy split workspace, precise line art.
directions.screen: Thermal simulation title Which material keeps heat in? Two virtual vessels labelled Fabric and Foil, starting at 60 °C. Independent variable Insulation, controls Same volume and Same start temperature. Right predicted cooling lines and Run simulation button. Footer Model results may differ from real experiments.
directions.logo: Two overlapping outlined beakers form an open house-shaped frame with one warm test dot.

directions.title: Evidence engine
directions.tagline: Let the results change your mind.
directions.style: Paper #F0E8D5, ink #263F54, rust #B65738. Bold three-stage horizontal workflow with graph-paper plotting area and humanist sans.
directions.screen: Three visible stages Predict, Test, Explain. Simulation Pendulum length. Centre pendulum with length slider and fixed mass. Right simulated period-versus-length results table: 0.25 m / 1.00 s, 0.50 m / 1.42 s, 1.00 m / 2.01 s, 1.50 m / 2.46 s, 2.00 m / 2.84 s. Define period as one complete back-and-forth swing. Bottom reflection My prediction and What the model showed. Button Run another trial.
directions.logo: A pendulum arc crosses a small graph axis, forming a compact dynamic T mark.

name: Number Kitchen
purpose: A virtual kitchen for quantities, fractions, measurement and money, with teacher-selected concepts and difficulty and optional physical measuring, sorting and sharing.
guardrail: Use metric units and Australian dollars. Arithmetic and fractional pictures must agree. This is a maths game, not a recipe recommendation.

directions.title: Little prep bench
directions.tagline: A little cooking. A lot of thinking.
directions.style: Cream #F6E9CF, tomato #B64935, sage #819879. Tactile overhead kitchen worktop with large clear rounded numerals.
directions.screen: Heading Share the pizza fairly. One pizza divided into 4 equal quarters and four plates. Task Give each person one quarter. Fraction 1/4 clearly shown. Bottom Try sharing and Explain buttons. Teacher task: Equal parts. Simple uncluttered layout for young children.
directions.logo: A quarter-circle pizza slice and a measuring spoon together form a cheerful N-shaped mark.

directions.title: Recipe notebook
directions.tagline: Mix, measure and make sense of maths.
directions.style: Paper #F2E5CC, deep blue #315170, lemon #DDBE56. Illustrated recipe notebook spread with handwritten quantity annotations and friendly serif titles.
directions.screen: Task Double the fruit mix. Recipe For 2: 1 banana, 2 strawberries; For 4: 2 bananas, 4 strawberries. Large draggable ingredient illustrations and a two-column recipe table. Buttons Check quantities and Show my thinking. Teacher concept Multiplication.
directions.logo: An open recipe book with two measuring-spoon page marks and one clear fraction slash.

directions.title: Fair-share café
directions.tagline: Something tasty to figure out.
directions.style: Pale peach #F4DFCD, dark teal #24595B, salmon #C9755B. Flat cut-paper neighbourhood café, menu-board typography and generous touch controls.
directions.screen: Counter challenge Three friends, six muffins. Six clearly countable muffins and three plates with two each. Prompt How many on each plate? Large number selector 2. Bottom Share again and Explain. Teacher task Equal groups. No time pressure or competitive score.
directions.logo: A café cup seen from above is split into three equal segments, its handle forming a small speech tail.

directions.title: Measure lab
directions.tagline: Big ideas in small measures.
directions.style: Cool milk #F0F0DF, forest #275747, ochre #CCA346. Montessori-like translucent measurement vessels, clean geometric type and pale tiled workspace.
directions.screen: Heading Make 500 mL. Clearly marked jug with 250 mL already filled, empty target outline at 500 mL. Two identical 250 mL cups. Prompt How much more? Large answer 250 mL and Pour a cup button. Footer Try it with classroom measuring cups.
directions.logo: A measuring jug silhouette contains a simple half-full line and two clear measurement ticks.

directions.title: Market kitchen
directions.tagline: Work it out, then dish it up.
directions.style: Canvas #EFE5D2, plum #573C4F, muted orange #D3914D. Market stall labels, bold chalk-like headers and flat produce illustration.
directions.screen: Task Buy ingredients with A$10. Apples A$3, bread A$4, carrots A$2 shown in a basket. Clear Total A$9 and Change A$1. A row of tactile Australian-dollar number tokens without detailed currency reproduction. Buttons Check the change and Try another basket.
directions.logo: A market basket contains three simple ingredient shapes whose handles form an equals sign.

name: StoryChirps
purpose: Children arrange picture sequences, record retellings and listen back to improve clarity, with teacher prompts and a private classroom collection; the same pictures can support different stories.
guardrail: No public sharing, follower counts, automated accent scores or single correct story. Make recording and listening clear and age appropriate.

directions.title: Picture parade
directions.tagline: Little pictures. Stories in your voice.
directions.style: Butter #F5E4B9, blue #315B76, coral #CB7257. Large cut-paper picture cards, rounded typography and clear audio controls.
directions.screen: Three reorderable picture cards: a child finds a seed, plants it, sees a sprout. Heading Tell your story. Numbered positions 1 2 3, large Record and Listen back buttons. Teacher prompt What happened first? Small Private classroom collection label.
directions.logo: Three small picture squares become a bird wing beside a round speech-bubble body.

directions.title: Story nest
directions.tagline: Every voice has a story.
directions.style: Pale sage #E0E8D0, dark green #3E573E, ochre #CCAA51. Soft illustrated nest metaphor, linen story stage and warm serif headings.
directions.screen: Four picture tiles around a central story area: umbrella, puddle, dog, sunny sky. Heading What could happen? A child-selected order along bottom. Large microphone control Tell it your way and playback Listen again. Prompt Who is your story for? Private collection indicator.
directions.logo: Two open speech bubbles nest together around a tiny bird-shaped centre.

directions.title: Sound postcards
directions.tagline: Tell it. Hear it. Tell it again.
directions.style: Sky #DDEAF0, brick #B4503D, paper #F9F0DA. Illustrated postcards with printed stamps and broad humanist type.
directions.screen: Two large picture postcards of the same park on a windy and calm day. Heading A story about the park. Recording waveform beneath pictures, controls Record, Stop, Listen. Prompt Add a detail your listener needs. Footer Saved to our classroom.
directions.logo: A postcard corner folds into a small bird beak, with three short sound lines.

directions.title: Little story stage
directions.tagline: Same pictures. Your own story.
directions.style: Cream #F1E3CD, aubergine #573F58, orange #C38A50. Paper theatre with restrained curtain shapes and friendly bold display lettering.
directions.screen: A paper theatre contains three picture panels: missing hat, windy tree, laughing child. Bottom reorder tray and big Record my story button. Heading What happens next? Side teacher prompt Describe where it happens. Listen back control and private classroom badge.
directions.logo: An open theatre curtain forms two bird wings around a central speech oval.

directions.title: Voice trail
directions.tagline: Find the words for what happens next.
directions.style: Ivory #F5EEDD, teal #215655, yellow #D6B447. Curved sequence trail with expressive flat illustrations and very clear sans lettering.
directions.screen: A winding trail links three big scene tiles: build a kite, take it outside, kite lands in a tree. Heading First, next, then... Teacher prompt Make the order clear. Large record button at trail end and playback strip across bottom. No correct-answer markers.
directions.logo: A gently curving audio line connects three picture dots and finishes in a small bird profile.

name: Plot a Place
purpose: Students create maps of classrooms, imaginary islands and neighbourhoods using symbols, directions, landmarks and simple scale; they exchange navigation challenges and explain how places meet needs.
guardrail: Include a map key and direction cues. Use simple consistent scale where shown. Tap-to-place alternatives should accompany dragging.

directions.title: Mapmakers’ desk
directions.tagline: Make a map. Make a way.
directions.style: Paper #F0E5CC, sea #39667B, ochre #CBA14B. Tactile mapmaking desk, cut-paper landmarks and atlas serif headings.
directions.screen: Create an island map with beach, bridge, forest and village on a simple grid. Left symbol palette; right Map key. North arrow and scale 1 square = 100 m. Heading Build your island. Buttons Place landmark and Set a route.
directions.logo: A folded map forms an angular P with a small circular location cutout.

directions.title: Little town planner
directions.tagline: Build places with a purpose.
directions.style: Pale mint #DFE9D9, brick #B75A3D, ink #354B51. Friendly flat town planning board and chunky accessible type.
directions.screen: Top-down neighbourhood with school, park, library and crossing. Heading What does our neighbourhood need? Side panel Place a landmark with three symbols; map key and north arrow. Bottom prompt Explain why you put it there. Button Add a place.
directions.logo: Three simple building blocks nest within a map-pin silhouette.

directions.title: Island atlas
directions.tagline: There’s a world in your next map.
directions.style: Seafoam #D3E7DF, navy #2D4966, sand #DDBB75. Beautiful illustrated island atlas, restrained contour lines and editorial typography.
directions.screen: An imaginary island with contour shapes, river, bridge and lookout. Heading Guide a friend to the lookout. Route markers Start, Bridge, Lookout. Right panel Directions with two numbered instructions, map key beneath. Button Try my route. Scale 1 square = 100 m.
directions.logo: Two flowing island contours form a P, with a tiny compass-point notch.

directions.title: Classroom compass
directions.tagline: Start here. Find your way.
directions.style: Chalk #F3EEDC, deep green #315747, terracotta #B77550. Overhead classroom floor-plan with tactile furniture symbols and large friendly labels.
directions.screen: Map of a classroom with door, reading corner, tables and shelves. Heading Map our classroom. Symbol tray and key, north arrow. Selected reading corner shows Why here? Keep it away from the noisy door. Button Give a friend directions.
directions.logo: Four rounded compass points surround a small square classroom with an open doorway.

directions.title: Route swap
directions.tagline: Your map. Someone else’s adventure.
directions.style: Linen #EFE9D7, cobalt #36588B, coral #CD795B. Graphic route puzzle with coloured paths, transit-map clarity and bold numerals.
directions.screen: Two panels My map and Your challenge. Map shows school, bridge, oval and library, with a key and north arrow. Task Start at school. Go east to the bridge. Cross the bridge, then go north to the library. Buttons Test directions and Share with class. No public sharing.
directions.logo: Two interwoven route lines form opposing arrows around one destination dot.

name: Clue Canopy
purpose: Illustrated story mysteries where students infer motives, predict and resolve contradictions by selecting textual clues and explaining reasoning through speech, drawing or writing.
guardrail: Evidence must come from visible story text. Do not reward guesses without reasons. Offer spoken, drawn and written explanations.

directions.title: Forest casebook
directions.tagline: Find the clue. Explain the why.
directions.style: Parchment #F0E5CB, forest #284D3E, amber #CEA14D. Illustrated forest mystery and printed casebook, readable book typography.
directions.screen: Story excerpt: Mia said she had stayed inside. But wet leaves clung to her shoes. Illustrated veranda on left, excerpt on right with wet leaves clung to her shoes highlighted. Question What suggests Mia went outside? Buttons Select a clue, Speak, Draw, Write.
directions.logo: A magnifying glass handle becomes a tree trunk beneath a canopy shaped like an open book.

directions.title: Evidence board
directions.tagline: Good readers follow the evidence.
directions.style: Paper #EFE2C8, ink #354657, brick #AD5039. Restrained detective pinboard with evidence threads and strong editorial type.
directions.screen: Story: The lunchbox was empty. Leo brushed crumbs from his jumper and looked away. Question What might Leo be hiding? Two highlighted textual clues pinned beside an illustration. Bottom My explanation with Speak, Draw, Write options. Button Connect a clue.
directions.logo: Two overlapping speech notes joined by a small evidence dot form a compact C.

directions.title: Canopy theatre
directions.tagline: Read between the leaves.
directions.style: Sage #DEE6CD, plum #513B50, ochre #C0A04D. Layered illustrated forest stage, large story panels and elegant friendly serif.
directions.screen: Illustrated character waiting at a bridge. Visible text: Noor packed a torch, though the walk was meant to end before sunset. Question What might happen next? Right Evidence from the story selection showing packed a torch. Bottom Explain your prediction with voice, drawing or text.
directions.logo: An open book arches into a leaf canopy with a small eye-shaped negative space below.

directions.title: Margin detective
directions.tagline: There’s more in the story.
directions.style: Warm white #F4EDE1, petrol #275760, muted orange #CB8B58. Beautiful annotated reading page, underlines and spacious margin reasoning cards.
directions.screen: Reading page: Ava offered Ben her umbrella. She kept glancing at his soaked notebook. Question Why might Ava offer the umbrella? Highlight soaked notebook. Margin My reason linked to highlighted phrase. Three controls Record, Sketch, Write. Button Save my explanation.
directions.logo: A curved annotation bracket and magnifying lens create a distinctive C-shaped reading mark.

directions.title: Clue trail
directions.tagline: Follow your hunch. Bring a reason.
directions.style: Sand #EBDCC0, olive #50613F, storm #3B6070. Adventure trail through illustrated story fragments, tactile chapter markers.
directions.screen: Three story panels show a missing scarf, an open gate and a branch. Text includes A strip of red wool fluttered on the low branch. Question Where would you look next? A selected text clue and an explanation area remain visible. Buttons Choose evidence and Explain.
directions.logo: A dotted trail curls into a question mark beneath a single leaf-shaped canopy.

name: SwitchSide Stories
purpose: Teacher-guided illustrated social scenarios where children explore different perspectives, try responses and discuss consequences, allowing several reasonable answers.
guardrail: No points, moral ranking, winner, single correct response, good-child labels or automated emotion judgement. Invite discussion and uncertainty about how others feel.

directions.title: Two windows
directions.tagline: One moment. More than one view.
directions.style: Pale peach #F4DFD1, green #355D4B, gold #CFAC56. Two equal story windows with expressive picture-book figures and calm round type.
directions.screen: Playground scene: one child wants to join a game, another is unsure how to include them. Two equal panels What could Sam be thinking? and What could Riley be thinking? Button Switch view. Bottom teacher prompt What could they try? Several response cards without ticks.
directions.logo: Two overlapping open windows form opposing speech bubbles with equal visual weight.

directions.title: Story seesaw
directions.tagline: Try another side of the story.
directions.style: Sky #DFE9E9, brick #B7654B, ink #344655. Paper-cut story playground, centred balanced composition and large friendly text.
directions.screen: Two children both reach for the same marker. Heading We both need the blue one. A large Switch sides control below scene. Three response cards Take turns, Find another blue, Draw together. Prompt What might happen next? No correct-answer colouring.
directions.logo: A gentle seesaw beam balances two distinct speech bubbles at equal height.

directions.title: Conversation quilt
directions.tagline: Make room for another point of view.
directions.style: Linen #F1E6D4, muted plum #655062, sage #92AA91. Quilt-like illustrated story panels, soft stitched dividers and readable serif titles.
directions.screen: Four panels depict a group building a model and one child whose idea is not heard. Heading Everyone has an idea. Select a person to hear their view. Bottom teacher discussion strip What could help everyone join in? Buttons Try a response and Talk together.
directions.logo: Four differently shaped fabric-like patches assemble into a single open speech bubble.

directions.title: Pause and play
directions.tagline: Pause the moment. Explore the choices.
directions.style: Warm white #F3ECDE, teal #2A595D, apricot #D4996D. Simple theatre storyboard with one paused scene, broad controls and restrained poster typography.
directions.screen: A paused illustrated scene of two children disagreeing over game rules. Heading We had different rules. Left Hear this view, right Hear this view. Bottom choices Ask what each person expected, Agree on a rule, Ask for help. Button Try this response. Teacher-led discussion label.
directions.logo: Two pause bars gently turn into facing conversation profiles, linked by an open arc.

directions.title: Paths together
directions.tagline: Different choices. A conversation to share.
directions.style: Pale sage #E0E7D7, dark blue #375466, warm yellow #D6B858. Branching illustrated paths without finish flags or rankings, warm humanist type.
directions.screen: Story scene: a child wants to work alone during a group task. Three possible response paths Invite a small role, Ask what they need, Make a plan together. Heading What could the group try? Right consequence preview with neutral description. Button Discuss this choice.
directions.logo: Two separate curved paths join briefly then continue, forming a balanced S-shaped conversation symbol.

name: Instruction Impossible
purpose: Students write directions for a literal character; missing steps and ambiguity have visible consequences, leading to revision and peer challenges.
guardrail: Focus on writing clear instructions, not coding syntax. Show recoverable funny consequences and a concrete revision.

directions.title: Literal little robot
directions.tagline: Say what you mean. See what happens.
directions.style: Butter #F1E1B8, petrol #28505C, orange #C57947. Matte toy robot workshop, bold rounded headings and numbered instruction cards.
directions.screen: Friendly robot stands beside a box. Draft instructions 1. Go to the box. 2. Put it there. The robot pauses with question Where is there? Right editor highlights there. Suggested revision area Write a clearer step. Buttons Run instructions and Try again.
directions.logo: A square robot face has a question-mark antenna and a small numbered-page corner.

directions.title: Parcel panic
directions.tagline: Clear steps. Unexpected adventures.
directions.style: Canvas #EDE0C7, brick #B95D40, navy #345068. Illustrated parcel depot, stamped directions and crisp utilitarian sans.
directions.screen: A literal courier carries a parcel to the wrong table. Instructions visible: Take the parcel to the table. Two tables labelled Round table and Square table. Heading Which table did you mean? Editable revised step Take the parcel to the round table. Run again button.
directions.logo: A folded parcel ribbon becomes a winding arrow with a small purposeful question bend.

directions.title: Paper pilot
directions.tagline: Write it. Try it. Make it clearer.
directions.style: Sky #DDE9ED, olive #5A653E, terracotta #BB7353. Folded-paper world, numbered flight-path cards and editorial serif headers.
directions.screen: A paper character at a bridge follows step Turn left before the bridge and heads into a flower bed. Split screen instruction list and animated result. Heading Check the order of your steps. Revised step Cross the bridge, then turn left. Buttons Test and Swap challenge.
directions.logo: A folded paper plane becomes a directional arrow wrapped around a small exclamation-shaped crease.

directions.title: Kitchen chaos
directions.tagline: The next step is in your hands.
directions.style: Cream #F5E4C7, green #37604B, rust #BA6546. Playful clean kitchen illustration, recipe-card instruction editor and warm broad type.
directions.screen: A literal character places a whole closed jar on bread after reading Put jam on the bread. Task Add the missing steps. Editor lines Open the jar, Use a spoon to take some jam, Spread the jam on the bread. Buttons Test my instructions and Compare.
directions.logo: A spoon-shaped arrow traces three clear steps around a square instruction card.

directions.title: Direction workshop
directions.tagline: Make instructions someone can follow.
directions.style: Paper #EEE7D5, cobalt #3F5D86, marigold #D3AE48. Graphic obstacle workshop with grid floor and large printed step numerals.
directions.screen: A friendly character waits on a grid beside blocks. Writing panel: Walk forward. Turn. Pick it up. Ambiguous words highlighted. Heading Be precise about where and how. Clear revision field Turn right at the blue block. Buttons Run, Revise, Exchange challenge.
directions.logo: Three offset numbered-step shapes form a clear turning arrow, with a small gap before the final step.

name: Edit Echidna
purpose: Teachers assign one revision goal; students improve their own writing, compare versions and explain their changes through focused challenges.
guardrail: Show meaningful student revision, not automatic rewriting or correction overload. Preserve student authorship and focus on exactly one goal.

directions.title: Small steps studio
directions.tagline: A stronger story, one change at a time.
directions.style: Warm paper #F4E9D2, teal #2D5658, ochre #D1A950. Gentle echidna line mascot, spacious writing desk and friendly serif headings.
directions.screen: Teacher goal Make the order clearer. Side-by-side My first version: We ate lunch. We walked to the park. My new version: First, we walked to the park. Then we ate lunch. Highlight only sequencing changes. Bottom I changed... reflection. Button Save my revision.
directions.logo: A simple echidna silhouette whose three quills are short pencil strokes, with a tiny rounded snout.

directions.title: Revision garden
directions.tagline: Give your words room to grow.
directions.style: Pale sage #E0E8D3, forest #36533D, clay #BA7854. Growing sentence stems, calm garden margin illustration and clear humanist type.
directions.screen: Goal Add one supporting detail. Student draft The garden was busy. Revised The garden was busy. Bees moved between the yellow flowers. A single added sentence highlighted. Small echidna in margin, prompt How does your detail help the reader? Buttons Compare and Explain.
directions.logo: An echidna profile with three leaf-shaped quills growing from an underline.

directions.title: Before and better
directions.tagline: See what a thoughtful edit can do.
directions.style: Cream #F0E4CE, ink #3D4D65, coral #C87964. Editorial split-page comparison with bold typographic change markers.
directions.screen: Heading Help your reader picture it. Teacher goal Add a specific detail. Before: The dog ran away. After: The muddy dog squeezed through the gap in the fence. Only the new details highlighted. Right reflection box What did you add, and why? Button Keep this version.
directions.logo: Two overlapping page shapes form an echidna back, with one small orange revision stroke.

directions.title: Writer’s workbench
directions.tagline: Your words. Your next good change.
directions.style: Linen #EBE4D6, bottle #2F564A, amber #CAA056. Tactile writing tools, one focused margin prompt, rounded slab-serif titles.
directions.screen: Student paragraph on left. Single goal Explain your reason. Original I think our class should have a garden. New sentence We could observe insects and measure how plants grow. Right one-task card Add a reason that supports your idea. Bottom Compare versions and Explain my change.
directions.logo: A pencil lies across a minimal echidna-shaped underline, its quills echoing three editorial marks.

directions.title: Revision trail
directions.tagline: One clear goal. A better next draft.
directions.style: Pale blue #DEE7E7, plum #59424F, mustard #C5A346. Three clear stepping-stone stages Read, Revise, Reflect, with fine echidna tracks.
directions.screen: Active stage Revise. Teacher goal Make the ending clearer. Draft ending Then we went home. Revised ending We went home with wet shoes and a plan to return to the creek. Bottom reflection How does the new ending connect to your story? Buttons View first draft and Save my explanation.
directions.logo: Three small quill-like marks follow a curved path into a compact echidna nose, suggesting progress without a trophy.
